findings.title: BehavioralProfile call site in server code is not covered by any task
findings.description:
Task 2.1 makes `leadership_weight` and `momentum_weight` required, and Task 2.2 updates call sites only under `tests/`. `simulation.py` builds `BehavioralProfile` from `ProfileConfig` with the six existing fields, so it raises `TypeError` once 2.1 lands.

- **Unmet requirement:** the slice's "backward-incompatible by design; all affected tests are updated" and "all tests green" criteria. 2.2's verify step (`pytest tests/`) cannot be met by following the task as written if any test exercises this builder.
- **Missing decision:** `ProfileConfig` (`src/migratory_server/config.py:51`) has no herding fields, and its parser already uses `data.get(..., default)` for the flocking weights. Without direction, a junior implementer will likely hard-code `0.0` at the call site, which the project's no-silent-fallback rule forbids.
- **Stale context:** the frontmatter `projectState` ("80 tests passing", engine only) does not mention the server package. 2.2 also omits `tests/test_simulation.py:65` and `tests/test_entities.py:27` from its named files; only the catch-all search bullet covers them.

Fix: add a task after 2.1 that extends `ProfileConfig` and its parser with the two fields, passes them through in `simulation.py`, and updates the config and simulation tests. Refresh `projectState`.

findings.title: Batch spawn merges AgentState arrays by hand and will leave `leadership` out of sync
findings.description:
Task 1.1 updates `create()`, `add_agent()` and `remove_agent()`, but `EntityManager.spawn_population` concatenates `positions`, `velocities`, `accelerations` and `profile_indices` field by field. After 1.1, a batch spawn leaves `state.leadership` at its old length while `count` grows.

- **Consequence:** `remove_agent()` will then `np.delete` an index beyond the end of the leadership array, which should raise `IndexError` (not run here), and `LeadershipForce` would index out of bounds on any server-built state.
- **Unmet requirement:** the slice's "`add_agent()` and `remove_agent()` must also handle the new array" and its Integration Points promise of an extended `AgentState` usable by later slices.
- **Task 1.2 gap:** its "these use `AgentState.create()` so they should work without changes" bullet does not anticipate this path.

Fix: add a sub-item to 1.1 to concatenate `batch.leadership` in the merge, and a test in 1.2 asserting `leadership.shape == (count,)` after spawn and after spawn-then-remove.

findings.title: Convergence assertion in 5.2 is satisfied by the initial conditions
findings.description:
The criterion is that mean heading "converges toward the leaders' initial heading". Task 5.2 asserts only that the final mean heading has a positive x-component. Five of the 50 agents start at `[4.0, 0.0]`, so the population mean is already biased east at tick 0, and alignment roughly preserves mean velocity. The test would likely pass with `LeadershipForce` returning zeros.

Fix: assert on change, for example that the non-leader agents' mean eastward heading component at the end exceeds its initial value by a stated margin.

Task 5.3 has a related weakness: its assertion is an either/or (lines 160-161), which lets the implementer pick whichever metric happens to pass. Name one metric.

findings.title: LeadershipForce known-geometry test checks direction only
findings.description:
The criterion is "correct output for hand-constructed inputs". Task 4.2 asserts only that the force on agent 2 "biases toward agent 1's heading". The exact value is hand-computable: (0.1·[0,1] + 0.9·[1,0]) / 1.0 − [0,0] = `[0.9, 0.1]` at `leadership_weight=1.0`.

A normalisation bug such as dividing by neighbour count gives `[0.45, 0.05]`, which still passes the direction check and the "similar to plain averaging" uniform test.

Fix: assert `result[2] ≈ [0.9, 0.1]`, matching the exact-value check `MomentumForce` already gets in 3.2.

findings.title: Vectorisation requirement is not carried into any task
findings.description:
The slice requires "Both forces are vectorized within each agent's neighborhood — no nested Python loops". Task 4.1 writes the weighted average as `sum(velocity[i] * leadership[i]) / sum(leadership)`, which a junior implementer can reasonably read as a Python loop over neighbours. Nothing in 4.1 or the Section 6 verification states or checks the requirement.

Fix: add one sub-item to 4.1 requiring the neighbour computation to use NumPy array operations with no inner Python loop.

findings.title: Section 6 and Task 5.1 add weight without covering any criterion
findings.description:
- **Task 6.2** repeats the protocol-conformance checks already in 3.1, 3.2, 4.1 and 4.2. Cut it.
- **Task 6.3** commits "any remaining changes" as `docs: complete slice 102` after 5.4 has already committed everything. It will be an empty or checkbox-only commit. Cut it.
- **Task 6.1** is a full-suite run. Fold it into the verify step of 5.3, before the 5.4 commit.
- **Task 5.1** is a five-force smoke test with no assertion beyond "runs without error", and 5.2 already runs the same five forces through `tick()` for 300 steps. Merge it into 5.2.

findings.title: Commit steps are checkbox tasks, not `**Commit**:` markers
findings.description: Tasks 1.3, 2.3, 3.3, 4.3 and 5.4 are numbered checkbox tasks. Their placement is correct: each follows an implement-and-test pair at a green point and matches the slice's checkpoint list (Implementation Notes item 7). Converting them to plain `**Commit**:` lines would match the marker convention; no change to placement is needed.
